A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiMTok study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary material. Renumbered and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, grounding, image-understanding and Mask Perception results, together with mask-length and hierarchical-loss ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds small-object segmentation, boundary-quality and fine-tuned-model image-understanding results.

M1.justification: The tokenizer, vector quantization, causal token structure, hierarchical mask loss, three-stage training, mask/box ordering and optional SAM refinement remain unchanged. The new statement that the tokenizer and de-tokenizer use standard Transformer layers clarifies implementation.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds a dedicated small-object evaluation scenario within RefCOCO/+/g, targeting objects occupying less than 4% of an image. The source datasets, training coverage and other evaluation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark comparisons is unchanged. The new fine-grained analyses reuse PSALM, already evaluated in v1; the added MME row evaluates the authors' fine-tuned variant.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce the small-object selection threshold, covering 12.8% of samples, boundary F1 on RefCOCO validation, and an additional fine-tuned configuration on MME. Existing protocols remain stated as before. The new segmentation-only fine-tuning description conflicts with the retained mixed-general-data recipe in Section 4.3, so an actual training-recipe change cannot be established.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds targeted checks of small-object accuracy and boundary fidelity, addressing potential weaknesses of decoding without original-image features. Table 7 additionally examines general-understanding retention after fine-tuning. Existing mask-length, hierarchical-loss and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged. New results include small-object RefCOCO validation cIoU of 67.15 versus PSALM's 64.50, boundary F1 of 0.927 versus PSALM's 0.936, and seven fine-tuned MME scores. For example, the new fine-tuned posters score is 57, while the retained base-model score is 164; this is an added configuration comparison, not a revised base-model result.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), causal factorization, hierarchical-loss definition, Gaussian-label construction and SAM-refinement formulation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims about compact hierarchical tokens, segmentation and grounding performance, and preserved general understanding remain. v2 highlights visual chain-of-thought in the contribution list, but the same mask-before-box finding and interpretation already appear in v1 Section 4.8.1.

C2.justification: New Appendix A identifies fixed token lengths, dependence on referring prompts and fine-detail limitations. Appendix F discusses small-object weaknesses and missing multi-scale features. Section 4.7 adds a data-bias explanation for fine-tuned MME losses and makes the existing tentative attribution of general-understanding losses more categorical.

D1.justification: v2 discloses Nvidia A800 usage of 192, 1920 and 640 GPU-hours for the three stages, clarifies Transformer components, and replaces the promised Mask Perception release with a dataset access link. The abstract now advertises code rather than code and models; the PDFs do not establish whether model availability actually changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zou et al., 'Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once,' as reference [86] in Section 2. The remaining related-work taxonomy and research positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and emphasis edits, including clearer discrete-token terminology and highlighting the existing visual chain-of-thought interpretation. Two supplementary sections are inserted and subsequent appendices relettered; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the small-object results table and a row to Table 7. Existing figures and tables are repositioned, including Figure 2 and appendix visualizations and prompt tables, with limited caption and spacing changes. The original plotted trends and qualitative examples remain.

improvement.justification: The added fine-detail tests and fine-tuned MME results quantify limitations absent from v1's reporting. Explicit limitations and compute/data-access details further improve transparency. These are useful, bounded gains, although capability-preservation claims remain broad despite the new MME losses, and the fine-tuning data descriptions are inconsistent.
